stem:
Kavya looks at the diagram of Shape $P$ and Shape $Q$. Both are built from the same $8$ unit squares, side-aligned with no gaps. Shape $P$ is a $2$-by-$4$ rectangle. Shape $Q$ is an L-shape made by moving squares.

Which claim correctly compares area and perimeter?

options.text: Area and perimeter both stay the same for every rearrangement of the $8$ squares.
Changing the arrangement creates the $8$ unit squares.
Area stays the same because both shapes use $8$ unit squares, but the perimeter can change.
Only Shape $P$ has an area, because it is a rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Same 8 unit squares keep the same area; rearranging changes how many outer edges are exposed, so perimeter can change. Claiming both stay fixed, reversing cause, or restricting area to rectangles miss that.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as Shape P 2-by-4 rectangle and Shape Q L-shape from the same 8 unit squares.
